overall: The AG found the Authority violated the Open Meeting Law by holding January 10 and February 14, 2012 executive sessions on Forest Road for an improper purpose, and ordered release of those minutes within 30 days.

allegations.summary: Authority allegedly convened in executive session on Forest Road at its January 10 and February 14, 2012 meetings for an improper purpose.
allegations.key_passage: However, its executive session discussions regarding the Forest Road property were not proper under Purpose 3 because the Authority did not discuss any litigation, pending or otherwise.

allegations.summary: Discussion of the Forest Road property's development was not a permissible Purpose 6 real-property topic, so those executive sessions were improper.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the Authority should not have held these discussions in executive session during its January 10 and February 14, 2012 meetings.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Authority was not forthcoming when asked at the January 10, 2012 meeting about the executive session's purpose.
allegations.key_passage: Following our review, we find that the Authority violated the Open Meeting Law by convening in executive session for an improper purpose.

allegations.summary: Meeting notice headings 'Forest Road' and 'Legal Issues- Forest Road' were reviewed as to whether they stated all subjects of the executive session.
allegations.key_passage: The headings, "Forest Road" and "Legal Issues- Forest Road," fell short of the requirement that the Authority state "all subjects that may be revealed without compromising the purpose for which the executive session" will be called.

allegations.summary: The chair did not declare that an open meeting would be detrimental to the litigating or negotiating position, and did not state whether the body would reconvene in open session.
allegations.key_passage: In addition, the Chair failed to make the statement required by both Purpose 3 and 6 that an open meeting would have a detrimental effect on the litigating or negotiating position of the public body.

allegations.summary: The January 10 and February 14, 2012 executive session minutes were reviewed and found insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: We note that these minutes were not sufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: Executive session minutes from the two meetings were withheld from the public after the sessions were improper.
allegations.key_passage: Because we find, and the Authority admits, that there was no lawful purpose for the January 10 and February 14, 2012 executive sessions, we order the Authority to release the minutes from and any documents used during those meetings

remedy: Within 30 days, review the January 10 and February 14, 2012 executive session minutes and documents and release them unless attorney-client privilege or a Public Records Law exemption applies.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law; future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
